title: Regression: false "Appears to have lost bonding, skipping this connect!" with Special Pairing Workaround since 2026.07.08 — lost readings
body: ## Summary Since updating to a nightly containing commit 7213241f4 ("OB1: add mac caching fix", July 8), users with **Special Pairing Workaround** enabled (Samsung setting) get bursts of: Appears to have lost bonding, skipping this connect! @ 1 ... @ 10 The bonding is NOT actually lost. The check misfires, connects are skipped, and readings are lost until the safety valve at 10 skips forces a connect, or the user re-pairs or restarts the app. Several users are reporting this (e.g. on Facebook groups), and reports will likely grow as more people update. I located the source of the problem myself and used Claude to help analyze the code history, gather the background details, and propose a possible fix. ## Root cause Commit 7213241f4 added to `onStartCommand` in `Ob1G5CollectionService.java`: ```java transmitterMAC = null; // clear on every service start automata(); // sequence logic ``` The chain that turns this into a false positive: 1. `isDeviceLocallyBonded()` starts with `if (transmitterMAC == null) return false;` — an unknown MAC is reported as "not bonded". 2. `onStartCommand` runs on every alarm wake-up and now clears the MAC every time, right before calling `automata()`. 3. The state reset above it only maps `BOND/PREBOND/DISCOVER/CONNECT` back to `SCAN` — **`CONNECT_NOW` is kept**. So `automata()` can enter `CONNECT_NOW` with a freshly cleared MAC and no `tryLoadingSavedMAC()` call on the way. 4. In `CONNECT_NOW`, with Special Pairing Workaround on, the guard fires: `wasBonded.equals(getTransmitterID()) && !isDeviceLocallyBonded()` → skip connect → missed reading. Repeats until `skippedConnects` reaches 10. Users without the workaround setting never run this check, which matches reports that only Samsung users with the setting enabled are affected. ## Testing from my sons live-rig (Samsung SM-F711B / Z Flip3, Android 15, Dexcom G7) I tested versions on the same afternoon (Aug 20), same sensor, same pairing: | Build | Result | |---|---| | 049ce18-2026.03.27 | clean (4 days, zero occurrences) | | c2a0ba1-2026.08.08 | skip bursts @1–@10 within hours | | f49d55f-2026.06.17 | clean | | f8b047f-2026.04.22 | clean | | 805ba04-2026.03.01 | clean | | back to c2a0ba1-2026.08.08 | skips return within 4 minutes | All clean builds predate the July 8 commit; the only commit in the regression window touching this code path is 7213241f4. Burst pattern in the log matches the code exactly: counts to @10 (the `skippedConnects < 10` valve), ~5 s between attempts, ~5 min between clusters (G7 connect cycle). Recovery that worked: forget BT pairing + re-pair (or app restart — see below). On G7 every sensor is a new bonded transmitter, so each sensor change re-arms the condition. ## Suggested fix Do not treat "MAC not known yet" as "bonding lost". Options: - Call `tryLoadingSavedMAC()` at the top of the `CONNECT_NOW` case (or inside `isDeviceLocallyBonded()`) so the cached MAC is restored before the check, or - Require `transmitterMAC != null` in the skip condition: ```java if (wasBonded.equals(getTransmitterID()) && transmitterMAC != null && !locallyBonded && skippedConnects < 10) { ``` Either keeps the original purpose of both the July 8 MAC-clearing fix and the lost-bonding guard. See proposed fix in 712eac9b uploaded to my repo ## Workaround for affected users until a fix ships - Try to disable "Special pairing workaround". Forget BT device and re-pair. OR - Rollback to recommended version for G7 - https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/releases/tag/2026.06.17 Logs: [1787486871-xDrip-log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31348328/1787486871-xDrip-log.txt) Screenshot of issue: | | | |--------|--------| Threads on facebook from users experiencing this error: https://www.facebook.com/groups/xdrip/permalink/1998405371546783/ https://www.facebook.com/groups/xdrip/permalink/1988820212505299/ https://www.facebook.com/groups/xdrip/permalink/1998636931523627/ _Originally posted by @olorinmaia in https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/discussions/4705_ Tagging @jamorham after discussing issue with @Navid200 - let me know if there is anything else I can contribute with here.

comments.body:
I started a new G7 sensor for my son on my test-rig (Galaxy flip z 5) now and quickly reproduced the issue with latest nightly after pairing. Seem to happen if you loose a reading or if you restart collector while scanning or just randomly. Only way to fix it seem to be forget BT pairing and re-pair then it starts connecting properly again until next time it happens. The first time I experienced this was directly after updating from 03.27 to 08.08 release while already running an active sensor.

I was not able to reproduce this issue after I updated the app with applied fix https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/commit/712eac9b0c678f4dc792ecc3060a6a70a5bdabdc - tried all of the above steps. I'm switching over this sensor to my son's live-rig so can't test any more as I've reverted to the [2026.06.17](https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/releases/tag/2026.06.17) release where this issue doesn't appear.

@jamorham This is being reported in the facebook group.  
I would work on fixing it.  But, I don't have a Samsung for recreating the problem and testing.

> [@jamorham](https://github.com/jamorham) This is being reported in the facebook group. I would work on fixing it. But, I don't have a Samsung for recreating the problem and testing.

I think you can recreate the issue by enabling that setting special pairing workaround if you can do so without putting yourself in harms way! I don't necessarily think a Samsung phone is needed.

If I enable the setting with our latest Nightly, I will experience the problem.  If I enable it with your fix, I will not experience the problem.  But, that would still not be a real world scenario.  There is no reason to enable the setting on a Pixel.

I accept that there is a problem with our current Nightly.  But, I would like someone who has a Samsung to test and open the PR.
Is there a reason you cannot open the PR?

Correct, and you have a very valid point. 

I can submit the PR as a draft but I was hoping to get an opinion from @jamorham on the proposed fix before doing so since this isn't something I'm able to test more right now due to lack of test equipment and I can't use my sons live rig for it either.

He will not merge it if he thinks it is a risk.
As long as you explain everything in the PR, I don't see any problem with opening a PR.  You can state in the PR to what extent you have tested it.
